title: AI agents, explained with houses and money
oneliner: An AI agent works like a buyer's agent or financial advisor: you state the goal, it does the exploring, comparing, and executing for you.
says: Two analogies: buying a home yourself means visiting locations and comparing amenities; a buyer's agent does all that and books the home for you. Exploring every investment option yourself versus a financial advisor identifying the right plan for you. AI agents work the same way - an intelligent framework that performs the tasks to achieve your business goal, instead of you executing each task yourself.
explained: The analogies isolate the defining property: delegation of a goal, not a task. You do not tell the advisor each click to make; you state the outcome and constraints, and they handle the search, comparison, and execution loop. That is exactly what separates an agent from a script - and it is why the earlier reels about orchestration, state, and tool selection exist: delegation only works if the agent can plan, remember, and act.

The analogies also quietly carry the governance point. You delegate to a buyer's agent because they are licensed and accountable; you check the advisor's work before signing. Enterprise agents need the same: bounded authority, audit trails, human sign-off on consequential steps - the substance of his governance and orchestrator reels.
takeaway: Agent = delegated goal pursuit. The trust model matters as much as the tech: bounded authority and human review on the steps that matter.
